item.title: NCD citizen surrenders firearm
item.description: A good citizen in the National Capital District has been commended by Commander for the National Capital District and Central Province, Benjamin Turi, for willingly surrendering an unlicensed firearm. Turi thanked Seven Mile Police Station Commander Inspector Henry Map and his officers after receiving the surrendered weapon—a .38 calibre revolver.
item.content:encoded:
A good citizen in the National Capital District has been commended by Commander for the National Capital District and Central Province, Benjamin Turi, for willingly surrendering an unlicensed firearm.

Turi thanked Seven Mile Police Station Commander Inspector Henry Map and his officers after receiving the surrendered weapon—a .38 calibre revolver.

While acknowledging the work of the police station commanders and officers across the command, Turi challenged them to increase public awareness regarding the ongoing gun amnesty program in their respective operational areas.

“Before we look elsewhere, I want to call on my police officers to inspect themselves and their circles, and to bring forward any illegal firearms they or their acquaintances may possess.

“The gun amnesty period has been extended to December 25, 2026, as per a media statement from Police Minister Sir John Pundari—a directive we are all expected to support to ensure illegal weapons are turned in. These offensive weapons will only lead to trouble,” Turi said.

He said that to date, two individuals in the NCD have voluntarily surrendered their firearms and others are likely to follow.

The gun amnesty program was launched on February 27, 2026, by Police Minister Sir John Pundari who has travelled throughout the country witnessing the surrender of illegal weapons, expressed satisfaction with the results and reiterated his public call for anyone still holding illegal firearms to turn them in.

item.title: Local gives back to help Island community
item.description: Krangket islanders, outside Madang Town will, for the first time, have two new jetties, thanks to one of their very own sons, Allan Los, who is the Provincial Administrator for Eastern Highlands. Mr Los provided financial assistance for the construction of the two jetties, plus 14 solar street lights around the island.
item.content:encoded:
Krangket islanders, outside Madang Town will, for the first time, have two new jetties, thanks to one of their very own sons, Allan Los, who is the Provincial Administrator for Eastern Highlands.

Mr Los provided financial assistance for the construction of the two jetties, plus 14 solar street lights around the island.

The islanders over the years have been sharing the local primary school jetty with the teachers and students.

One of the two jetties was officially opened for use recently by the founder of Madang Rural Development Foundation, Kurere Matanzana, during a small ceremony on the island.

In his remarks prior to cutting the ribbon to officially signal the jetty was ready for use, he said credit must be given where it's due.

Mr Matanzana said Mr Los has done one of the most honourable things by giving something back to his people.

"We are gathered here to celebrate your success story, and I would like to take this time to thank everyone who contributed to the successful construction of the two jetties, one of which we are going to open today. Whether you bought a bag of cement, helped carry stones, or contributed a kina, K10, or K20, all your efforts were worth it.

"What we are witnessing today is proof and testament of all your hard work. It i a testament of Mr Los' dream for you," he said.

Matanzana told the local people to take ownership of the infrastructures and also extended appreciation to the management of Krangket Primary School for allowing the community to use the school's jetty for so many years.

He also encouraged parents on the island to embrace education and to work in unity for their own good, stressing that human resource is very important to development.

He said that when people unite on small projects like the jetties, they can create bigger things in their communities.

He added, "It is my wish and my prayer that this spirit of unity must continue amongst you. We don’t have land to cultivate cocoa on the island. Thus, your human resource is your number one asset, so embrace education.

Ward one councillor in the Ambenob Local Level Government area, Trevor Fan, thanked the three clans on the island; Lonpain, Gedaged Damon and Imalan, for standing together to complete the jetties.

"This project is an initiative of Allan Los. He is not here today with us, but we want to extend our gratitude to him. He provided 70 per cent of the resources and support for the two jetties. Although he's been away from the island for many years due to work commitment, he hasn't forgotten his roots. We greatly appreciate him.

"I also appreciate all three clans on the island for your cooperation, which had made it possible for the project to be successfully completed. The unity amongst us made this project become a reality," Councillor Fan said.

Ward one village court magistrate, Yaling Baran, urged youths on the island to respect the infrastructures and to keep unlawful activities away from them.

Meanwhile, Mr Matanzana, on behalf of Madang Rural Development Foundation, also pledged a K3, 000 support to compliment the project.

He said MRDF will provide and install solar lighting on the jetties.

"I didn't contribute anything to the project, but because you have invited me to officiate at this gathering, I feel obliged to contribute, and I am now making this commitment," he said.

Matanzana explained that this will be made possible under MRDF's Sustainable Energy Program, with support from the Israeli Government.

item.title: CTPM retain open men’s title
item.description: The Corporate Touch Port Moresby Open Men’s Team (CTPM) have retained their national title after defeating NCD Touch at the Bisini Park. The national touch championships finals matches were played today to conclude this year’s edition in Port Moresby as host CTPM scooped up three of seven national titles.
item.content:encoded:
The Corporate Touch Port Moresby Open Men’s Team (CTPM) have retained their national title after defeating NCD Touch at the Bisini Park.

The national touch championships finals matches were played today to conclude this year’s edition in Port Moresby as host CTPM scooped up three of seven national titles.

After missing out in the finals last year in Lae, Morobe, the CTPM Open Men’s made a comeback retaining their open Mens title at this year’s championship.

This year’s team consisted of both veterans and fresh talents to the mix as they went on undefeated in all their pool matches and finals before the big game against NCD.

PNG elite and CTPM co-captain Kele Lessy said despite a strong match against NCD, their team gave their all to finish the tournament on top.

“It was a touch match for us but we held on tightly in defense and scored the final try to secure the title,” Lessy said.

It was a strong contest for the host team as NCD matched up to the same tune to put a fast-paced match at the Bisini Park.

Despite efforts made, CTPM’s Freddy Gelam cruised past NCD’s defense to score the winning try at full time to break the 5-all draw.

Footy veteran and Co-captain Eugene Eka said this year’s tournament had a lot of intensity coming from all teams however it was up to them to keep their pace up to retain the title. “We finished in the Open Mens semi-finals at the last year’s champs in Morobe but this year was a comeback for us. But it has also been really tough throughout the championship, it wasn’t easy competing against the other teams.

“This sport has grown as we saw the level of competitiveness brought in by the other associations and their teams, it shows that the code in growing,” he said.

Meanwhile, CTPM also defended their back-to-back titles from last year in the Open Mix and Junior U20 Boys division.

In the womens matches, Owan Touch Association dominated taking out the Junior U20 Girls, Open Womens and Senior Womens national titles while Kainantu Gateway Touch secured the Senior Mens title, all representing Eastern Highlands. The Senior Mix title was won by NCD over Gateway Touch.

Following the conclusion of the championships, Touch Federation PNG is expected to announce the next phase of its regional and national sanctioned tournaments in due time.

item.title: From Ireland to PNG: Fr. John Glynn at 90
item.description: Former teacher, chaplain and counsellor of Jubilee Catholic Secondary School, and founder of Wecare and YACA, Fr. John Glynn, celebrated his 90th birthday on Sunday. Born and raised in Ireland, Fr. John was educated by the Christian Brothers and later by the Vincentian Fathers before moving to Papua New Guinea in 1963.
item.content:encoded:
Former teacher, chaplain and counsellor of Jubilee Catholic Secondary School, and founder of Wecare and YACA, Fr. John Glynn, celebrated his 90th birthday on Sunday.

Born and raised in Ireland, Fr. John was educated by the Christian Brothers and later by the Vincentian Fathers before moving to Papua New Guinea in 1963.

For more than six decades, Fr. John has served communities in Papua New Guinea as a priest, teacher, chaplain and counsellor.

His life and ministry have been characterised by a deep commitment to young people, education, women, children and people experiencing hardship and vulnerability.

His contribution to Papua New Guinea extends well beyond the parish.

Fr. John also played a role in the early development of Digicel Papua New Guinea, assisting the company when it established operations in the country in 2007 and subsequently serving as a member of its board.

Over the years, Fr. John Glynn has touched countless lives through his service, compassion, mentorship and advocacy.

His work has crossed the boundaries of the church, education, business and community development, making him a respected figure among many communities in Papua New Guinea.

As he celebrates 90 years of life, his journey stands as a testament to a life devoted to service.

From Ireland to Papua New Guinea, and from the classroom to the parish, boardroom, and community, Fr. John Glynn has dedicated much of his life to helping others.

item.title: Dame Maria Kopkop calls on students to help build PNG’s future
item.description: Kopkop College Executive Director and Founder Dame Maria Kopkop has challenged the next generation of Papua New Guineans to use education, strong character, good health and responsible citizenship to help build the nation over the next 50 years. Dame Maria made the call during Kopkop College’s 51st Independence anniversary celebrations in Port Moresby, where students, teachers, parents, school man
item.content:encoded:
Kopkop College Executive Director and Founder Dame Maria Kopkop has challenged the next generation of Papua New Guineans to use education, strong character, good health and responsible citizenship to help build the nation over the next 50 years.

Dame Maria made the call during Kopkop College’s 51st Independence anniversary celebrations in Port Moresby, where students, teachers, parents, school management and members of the community gathered to reflect on Papua New Guinea’s journey since independence and look towards the country’s future.

She said education must go beyond academic results and certificates.

She stressed that students must develop the knowledge, values and skills needed to contribute positively to society.

“Education is more than just passing examinations and receiving certificates. Education teaches you how to think, how to solve problems, how to make wise choices, how to respect others, and how to contribute to your country,” she said.

Dame Maria said the young generation would face new challenges as Papua New Guinea moves towards its centenary of independence in 2075.

“You will inherit challenges that my generation may not have completely solved, but you will inherit opportunities that earlier generations could never have imagined.

"Science and technology will continue to change the world, new careers will emerge, climate change will challenge our communities, and our health system will need drastic, important solutions.” Mama Kopkop said.

She said academic achievement must be supported by good character, honesty, discipline, compassion and courage.

“Our country will need honest leaders, skilled professionals, innovative thinkers, entrepreneurs, teachers, doctors, engineers, and importantly, responsible citizens. That is why I say to you today, children. Stand strong in your education. Knowledge without character cannot build a strong nation.”

Dame Maria also urged students to take responsibility for their physical and mental well-being.

“Look after your health. A strong mind needs a healthy body. Eat wisely, exercise, avoid harmful habits, care for your mental well-being, and build relationships that bring goodness into your life.” she added.

Looking towards 2075, Dame Maria said many of the students attending the celebration today would become the leaders, professionals, parents and grandparents of the future.

“In 2075, when Papua New Guinea celebrates 100 years of independence, many of you sitting here today will be the leaders, professionals, parents, and grandparents looking back on the journey.”

She expressed hope that the students would play an active role in building a peaceful, educated, healthy and prosperous Papua New Guinea.

“My hope, children, is that you will see a peaceful, educated, healthy, and prosperous nation, and that you will be able to say, ‘We helped build that."

Meanwhile the Director also encouraged students to understand and respect Papua New Guinea’s history, including the cultures, traditions, knowledge and communities that existed long before independence.

She said the country’s future development must continue to recognise the importance of culture, family values and the contribution of communities to nation-building.

Maria emphasised that Kopkop College’s education philosophy places emphasis on academic excellence, cultural values, family and the development of each child’s individual potential and this pillars will continue to remain.

item.title: Teachers warned of fake TSC officers on Facebook
item.description: The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] has warned teachers, especially recent graduates and those in very remote locations, not to be fooled by scammers operating on social media platforms like Facebook. TSC Acting Chairman Maini Mike Ugaia issued the warning following reports that fraudsters are tricking teachers into paying fake “legal service fees” to secure employment.
item.content:encoded:
The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] has warned teachers, especially recent graduates and those in very remote locations, not to be fooled by scammers operating on social media platforms like Facebook.

TSC Acting Chairman Maini Mike Ugaia issued the warning following reports that fraudsters are tricking teachers into paying fake “legal service fees” to secure employment.

Ugaia clarified that the Commission does not charge any fees for its services, stating that there is no such thing as a legal service fee or administrative charge within the TSC and the Education Department.

The Commission is aware of a fraudulent Facebook profile operating under the name Guina Robin, which has been falsely claiming to be a TSC officer and misleading teachers.

To prevent further exploitation, the TSC is advising all teachers to avoid conducting official business on social media.

Teachers are also reminded that Commission officers are stationed on the ground in every province.

Teachers with employment queries or paperwork issues are urged to visit their local provincial education office to speak with genuine staff face-to-face.

The public and the teaching fraternity are urged to remain vigilant and report any suspicious individuals or payment demands to the police or the TSC head office.

item.title: Districts told to direct 10% funding to SMEs
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape says 10% of funding allocated to each district in Papua New Guinea is intended to support Small and Medium Enterprises [SMEs], helping local businesses establish, grow and create opportunities for people in rural communities. He says every district in Papua New Guinea has different economic opportunities and needs.
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister James Marape says 10% of funding allocated to each district in Papua New Guinea is intended to support Small and Medium Enterprises [SMEs], helping local businesses establish, grow and create opportunities for people in rural communities.

He says every district in Papua New Guinea has different economic opportunities and needs.

Some districts have strong potential in tourism, while others are better suited to agriculture, forestry, fisheries and other industries.

The Prime Minister was speaking at Government House after the swearing-in of the two vice ministers last week.

The Government’s approach is aimed at making it easier for people in rural areas to access support and participate in economic activity by ensuring that districts allocate funding to assist local SMEs.

Prime Minister James Marape says people seeking assistance for their businesses should approach their respective Members of Parliament and district administrations, rather than travelling to the Prime Minister’s Office, City Governors or national government departments seeking business funding.

He emphasized that district members have a responsibility to ensure local communities benefit from available SME support.

Where such funding is not being provided, he said, people have the right to hold their elected representatives accountable.

Prime Minister James Marape says there should be no excuse for districts failing to support their people.

He said instructions have been given to district members to assist local SMEs, with particular emphasis on agriculture and tourism, as well as creating opportunities for young people.

item.title: TSC rejects claims of teacher’s pay rise
item.description: The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] Acting Chairman, Maini Mike Ugaia, has strongly disapproved recent media statements made by the Papua New Guinea Teachers Association [PNGTA] President regarding a premature teachers' pay increase. Chairman Ugaia clarified that while discussions and initial submissions concerning the 2026–2028 log of claims have been presented to the Department of Personnel Ma
item.content:encoded:
The Teaching Service Commission [TSC] Acting Chairman, Maini Mike Ugaia, has strongly disapproved recent media statements made by the Papua New Guinea Teachers Association [PNGTA] President regarding a premature teachers' pay increase.

Chairman Ugaia clarified that while discussions and initial submissions concerning the 2026–2028 log of claims have been presented to the Department of Personnel Management [DPM], any proposed salary adjustments between the TSC and the PNGTA remain strictly subject to DPM approval.

“The statement circulated in the media is untrue and misleading.

“The PNGTA President is advised to withdraw these unauthorized claims immediately. Negotiations are a formal administrative process, and creating false expectations among our hard-working teachers disrupts the stability of our education sector.” Acting Chairman Ugaia said.

He said releasing unverified public declarations regarding a pay increase is both premature and highly unprofessional.

Teachers throughout Papua New Guinea are urged not to rely on speculative media coverage or external announcements regarding their terms and conditions.

TSC remains the sole legal employer and authoritative body responsible for teacher welfare and salary matters; consequently, all teachers should obtain official updates directly from the TSC headquarters or through authorized TSC Media Announcements.

“The Commission extends its appreciation to our nearly 70,000 teachers nationwide for their unwavering commitment and dedication to our students throughout this academic year.

“As we enter the final term of the school calendar, we wish you all the very best and continued success in your classrooms.” Acting chairman Ugaia said.

item.title: Court orders State to pay K52. 2 million compensation for Madang town land
item.description: A long- running Human Rights court case by landowners of the land on which Madang town sits, against the State; has finally come to a close after the National Court in Madang ruled that the plaintiffs, who are the ten landowner clans, be compensated justly.
